subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The fastest seismic body waves, which arrive first at a station, are:
options: Love waves, faster than P-waves
S-waves (secondary), slower than P
P-waves (primary/compressional)
Rayleigh waves, fastest surface waves
solution: P-waves are compressional and travel fastest, arriving before slower S and surface waves.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a variogram model, the sill and range represent which aspects of spatial variability?
options: Constant semivariance at all lags, implying no spatial correlation in the data
Semivariance vs distance. Sill = total variance. Range = correlation length
A linear semivariance increasing without bound, implying that no finite sill value exists
Semivariance that is undefined because the regionalized variable is purely random
solution: Variogram: γ(h) = ½E[(Z(x)-Z(x+h))²]. Spherical, exponential, Gaussian models. Nugget effect.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A rock retains 50% of its original parent isotope (half-life 1.3 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
options: 1.3 Gyr
2.6 Gyr
3.9 Gyr
0.65 Gyr
solution: 50% remaining ⇒ 1 half-lives ⇒ age = 1×1.3 = 1.3 Gyr.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How does porosity typically differ between the core and the damage zone of a fault zone?
options: Core: low porosity (gouge). Damage zone: high fracture porosity. Conduit-barrier
The fault core is the most porous part and the damage zone acts as a sealing barrier to flow
Porosity increases steadily and monotonically from the protolith toward the fault core
The entire fault zone has uniform porosity equal to the undeformed host rock's porosity
solution: Fault seal: clay smear, cataclasis. Juxtaposition seal. Membrane seal (capillary entry pressure).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which parameters are used to judge the quality of coal intended for coking?
options: Only the ash content of the raw coal as mined from the seam as it is produced
Moisture content and volatile matter alone in the as-received sample of the coal
Sulphur and phosphorus content of the coal as determined by ultimate analysis
Caking index (GRI), CRI (coke reactivity), CSR (coke strength after reaction)
solution: Coking: GRI >70 for good coking. CRI <25, CSR >65 for blast furnace coke.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Transmissivity T = K*b. For K=10 m/day, aquifer thickness b=20m:
options: T = 200 m2/day
T = 2000 m2/day
T = 2 m2/day
T = 0.5 m2/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What hardness value does the mineral apatite possess on the Mohs scale of hardness?
solution: Ca5(PO4)3(F,Cl,OH). Index mineral #5. Phosphate ore.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: U-shaped valleys, cirques, arêtes, horns, hanging valleys and moraines are landforms created by which agent?
options: Cone of sediment deposited where a mountain stream abruptly meets a plain at the foot of the mountain front
Narrow steep-sided valley produced by active river downcutting and vertical incision of the river bed
U-shaped valley, cirque, arête, horn, hanging valley, moraine (lateral, medial, terminal)
Sediment body deposited where a river enters a lake or sea and spreads out into the standing body of quiet water beyond
solution: Glacial: erosion (U-valley) and deposition (moraine, drumlin, esker, till).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In GIS, landslide susceptibility mapping commonly uses a weighted overlay of which factors such as slope, geology, rainfall, and land use?
options: Analysis that uses a single factor only, such as the slope gradient being considered alone
Weighted overlay: slope, geology, rainfall, land use, distance to faults
The distance to rivers only, while ignoring the geology and land use factors entirely
Rainfall intensity that is recorded over just a single monsoon season period
solution: Susceptibility: heuristic, statistical (logistic regression), deterministic (infinite slope). Machine learning.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Squeezing ground in a tunnel results from high stress acting on weak rock that deforms:
options: High stress in weak rock → plastic deformation. Invert struts needed
Rapid brittle failure of the rock mass with sudden and violent bursting
Continuous inflow of gas under high pressure from the tunnel face
High-permeability rock with steady seepage into the excavation
solution: Squeezing: ductile deformation. Caused by high overburden, weak rock (shale).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Lamprophyre: volatile-rich, porphyritic mafic igneous rock. Phenocrysts typically:
options: Quartz and alkali feldspar set in a coarse-grained equigranular matrix
Amphibole, biotite, or olivine in fine groundmass
Only quartz phenocrysts in a groundmass free of ferromagnesian minerals
Plagioclase and sanidine phenocrysts in a glassy volcanic matrix
solution: Lamprophyre: lamprophyric texture. Dark minerals as phenocrysts. Often associated with diamond pipes.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What does the principle of original horizontality state about the deposition of sediments?
options: Sediments deposited in horizontal layers
Sediments always deposited inclined at the angle of repose of the grains
Sediments deposited in curved and wavy surfaces following the basin contours
Sediments deposited in near-vertical sheets along active fault scarps
solution: Steno: tilted beds indicate post-depositional deformation.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The hornblende hornfels facies, a moderate-grade contact metamorphic facies, is characterized by which assemblage?
options: Contact metamorphism, moderate grade. Plagioclase + hornblende + cordierite
Low-grade contact metamorphism in which albite and epidote minerals remain stable
Regional metamorphism at high pressure typical of active subduction zones
Very high-grade contact metamorphism with pyroxene and no hydrous minerals remaining stable
solution: Hornfels facies: pyroxene-hornfels (high), hornblende-hornfels (medium), albite-epidote (low).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An ore body of 5 Mt has an average metal grade of 1%. The contained metal is about:
options: 25 kt
5 kt
100 kt
50 kt
solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 5 Mt × 1% = 50 thousand tonnes (kt).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 15 Mt
39 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 19.5 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral specimen of mass 78 g has a volume of 20 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
solution: SG = mass/volume = 78/20 = 3.9.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following measures is used to mitigate debris flows?
options: Contour bunding and terracing of the entire catchment area
Removing all vegetation to expose the source material
Check dams, deflection walls, sabo dams, early warning
Raising the channel bed with loose excavated spoil
solution: Debris flow: high velocity mixture of soil, rock, water. Runout distance analysis.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How does a mudstone differ from a shale in terms of fissility and bedding?
options: Lithified mud (silt + clay). Massive, no fissility
Coarse-grained rock of well-rounded quartz sand with cross-bedding
Fissile mudrock that splits easily along bedding planes into thin sheets
Volcanic rock with a glassy texture formed by rapid cooling of lava
solution: Mudstone vs shale: shale splits into thin layers (fissile).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Using a simplified proxy where calorific value ≈ 70 × fixed-carbon%, a coal with 40% fixed carbon has a calorific value of about:
options: 1400 kcal/kg
3500 kcal/kg
5600 kcal/kg
2800 kcal/kg
solution: CV ≈ 70 × 40 = 2800 kcal/kg (illustrative proxy).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which matrix and statistics, including the Kappa coefficient, are used to assess how accurately an image has been classified?
options: Reporting only a single overall accuracy percentage, without any per-class detail whatsoever being provided to the analyst
A simple visual comparison of the classified map with the original source imagery
Confusion matrix. Overall accuracy, producer's accuracy, user's accuracy. Kappa coefficient
Simply accepting the classification results, without performing any formal validation step whatsoever
solution: Confusion matrix: errors of omission (producer's) and commission (user's). Kappa: chance-corrected agreement.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A bed dipping at 30° shows a width of 30 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 30×sin30° ≈ 15 m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which geodetic technique can monitor crustal deformation with millimetre precision and track plate motion of a few centimetres per year?
options: Crustal deformation monitoring (mm precision). Plate motion ~cm/yr
Useful for navigation only, and is unsuitable for any scientific monitoring
Mapping of roads and property boundaries at the regional scales, nothing more
Photogrammetric mapping of the terrain, without using any ground-based receivers at all
solution: GPS: continuous GPS stations. Earthquake cycle: interseismic, coseismic, postseismic deformation.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How does fault gouge thickness typically vary with fault displacement and depth?
options: Increases with displacement and decreases with depth
Decreases with displacement and increases with depth below the surface
Remains constant regardless of the amount of slip or the depth of burial
Increases with depth but is unaffected by the total accumulated displacement
solution: Gouge thickness: t ∝ d^α (α≈0.5). Thicker at shallow depth (more brittle).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Rhyolite vs granite: same composition but:
options: Both rocks share the same texture because cooling rates are identical
Rhyolite is mafic while granite is felsic in bulk composition
Rhyolite: volcanic (fine-grained or glassy). Granite: plutonic (coarse-grained)
They differ in composition, rhyolite being richer in quartz and poorer in alkali
solution: Rhyolite: volcanic equivalent of granite. Same bulk composition. Texture differs due to cooling rate.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The fold shown in cross-section (beds arch upward about the axial plane) is a(n):
options: Monocline
Syncline
Graben
Anticline
solution: Upward-arching limbs dipping away from the axis define an anticline (oldest beds in core).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In the Hvorslev method of slug test analysis, hydraulic conductivity K is estimated using:
options: K = r²·ln(L/R)/(2·L·T₀). T₀ = time for 37% recovery
K = Q/(2πT) for steady radial flow toward the pumping well
K = T/S from the ratio of transmissivity to storativity
K = Q·W(u)/s evaluated at the match point of a type curve
solution: Hvorslev: for low-K formations. T₀ from semi-log plot of water level vs time.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+30+20) = 45%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Hydraulic conductivity of gravel vs clay:
options: Gravel has much higher K
Clay has higher K
They are equal
K depends only on temperature
solution: Gravel: K = 10^2 to 10^4 m/day. Clay: 10^-9 to 10^-5.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To extract 5 m³ of coal, 60 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 60/5 = 12 : 1.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A bed drops 10 m over a horizontal distance of 10 m. Its dip angle is about:
solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(10/10) ≈ 45°.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In which crystal system does the common mineral gypsum crystallize?
options: Cubic
Monoclinic
Triclinic
Orthorhombic
solution: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) — monoclinic. Hardness 2. Used in plaster.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A perched water table forms when a low-permeability lens creates:
options: Local saturated zone above region water table due to low-permeability lens
The regional water table surface that lies within a low permeability rock basin
An unsaturated interval lying directly beneath the regional water table
The piezometric surface of a deeply buried confined aquifer system
solution: Perched: clay lens creates local saturation. Limited yield. Shallow wells.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+35+15) = 42%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The GASP geobarometer, sensitive to pressure, is based on which net-transfer reaction?
options: Fe-Mg exchange between garnet and biotite giving an independent temperature estimate for the same rock
Grossular + Al₂SiO₅ + Quartz → Anorthite. Pressure-sensitive. Used with Grt-Bt thermometer
Aluminum saturation index of the bulk rock used to infer crystallization depth of the source magma
Si-content of phengite calibrated as a temperature-dependent barometer for low-grade pelitic schists
solution: GASP: Ca transfer. K = a_An³/(a_Grs·a_Ky²·a_Qz). P from equilibrium constant.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: For a geological cross-section to be considered balanced, what condition must be satisfied during restoration?
options: Conservation of bed length alone, ignoring any changes in the area of individual layers
Uniform horizontal shortening applied equally to every layer in the section without pinning
Conservation of bed length and area during restoration
Restoration with gap formation permitted in the synclines and fold crests of the section
solution: Balanced: no gaps or overlaps after restoration. Bed length and area preserved.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Basalt is best classified as which kind of igneous rock based on its texture and composition?
options: Coarse-grained intrusive rock rich in quartz and alkali feldspar
Chemical sedimentary rock precipitated from a saturated brine solution
Fine-grained extrusive mafic igneous rock
High-grade metamorphic rock showing distinct compositional banding
solution: Basalt is the fine-grained, dark, mafic rock formed from rapidly cooled lava.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A bed dipping at 30° shows a width of 40 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 40×sin30° ≈ 20 m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In deformed layered sequences, the sausage-like segmentation of competent beds known as boudinage indicates which strain condition?
options: Extension parallel to layering
Layer-parallel shortening during compression
Dextral shear across the rock mass
Strike-slip displacement along a fault plane
solution: Boudinage: layer stretched and broken into sausage-shaped blocks. Indicates extension along layering. Common in metamorphic rocks.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The width of a wave-cut platform is controlled primarily by the combined influence of which factors?
options: The width is controlled only by the rate of sea-level change
The width is controlled only by the rock resistance
The width is controlled only by the wave energy at the coast
Rate of sea-level change, rock resistance, wave energy
solution: Platform: wider in weak rock, high wave energy, stable sea level. Narrow: resistant rock, rapid sea-level change.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+35+10) = 50%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Vitrinite reflectance Ro% rank indicator: Ro < 0.5% is:
options: High-volatile bituminous coal with strong caking
Semi-anthracite of very low volatile matter
Lignite to sub-bituminous
Anthracite with maximum carbon content
solution: Lignite: Ro<0.5%. Sub-bit: 0.5-0.6%. Bituminous: 0.6-2.0%. Anthracite: >2.0%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In sedimentary geology, what does the provenance of a sediment refer to?
options: The mechanism of sediment transport from source to the basin of deposition
Source area of sediments (composition, age, tectonic setting)
The environment in which sediments are deposited and later lithified into rock
Post-depositional changes including compaction, cementation and dissolution of sediment
solution: Provenance: heavy mineral analysis, zircon U-Pb dating, paleocurrents.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the main advantage of Ar-Ar dating compared with the conventional K-Ar method?
options: Produces results much faster in the laboratory than the conventional K-Ar method on the same mineral separates
Single heating step or step heating for age spectrum. No need for separate K measurement
Considerably cheaper to run on bulk samples of the same rock that is being dated
More accurate ages for carbonate sediments and their cements in the section
solution: Ar-Ar: irradiation converts ³⁹K to ³⁹Ar. Step heating: age spectrum. Plateau age = undisturbed.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A P-wave travels at 8 km/s and arrives 20 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
options: 80 km
0.4 km
20 km
160 km
solution: distance = velocity × time = 8×20 = 160 km.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: To extract 15 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/15 = 3 : 1.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which logging techniques are used to determine in-situ rock properties in boreholes?
options: Gamma, resistivity, SP, caliper, sonic logging. In-situ rock properties
Only the measurement of core recovery and RQD from the recovered drill core
Only water level measurement in the borehole after completion
Geophysical profiling along the ground surface above the borehole
solution: Well logging: lithology, porosity, density, water quality. Acoustic televiewer: fractures.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which geophysical method offers high resolution but limited shallow depth penetration?
options: Ground penetrating radar. High resolution, shallow (<10m)
Electromagnetic sounding for deep crustal studies beyond 100 m depth
Gravity profiling to detect large density contrasts in the bedrock
Seismic refraction using hammer sources for deep oil exploration
solution: GPR: electromagnetic waves. Utility detection, void mapping, archaeology.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Seismic refraction — critical refraction:
options: Direct arrival that travels entirely within the surface layer after reflection at the boundary
Wave reflected from the interface returned to the surface at an angle equal to the incident angle
Surface wave travelling along the ground with velocity independent of layer properties
Head wave at critical angle (sin i_c = V₁/V₂). Refractor velocity V₂ from intercept time
solution: Refraction: first arrivals. Crossover distance. Layer thickness: h = (x_c/2)√((V₂-V₁)/(V₂+V₁)).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Groundwater occurrence in hard rock terrains is primarily controlled by:
options: Water in hard rocks occurs only within primary intergranular pores between mineral grains
Fracture-controlled. Weathered zone (shallow) + fractured zone (deeper). Yield variable
The rock mass behaves as a porous medium with a uniform and very high storage capacity
Yield is uniform everywhere and entirely independent of the fracture network
solution: Hard rock: only secondary porosity. Fracture zones, lineaments. High-yield wells along major fractures.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Goldschmidt's geochemical classification of elements groups Cu, Pb and Zn predominantly into which class?
options: Siderophile (Fe-loving, concentrated in the metallic core)
Chalcophile (S-loving, concentrate in sulfide phases)
Lithophile (O-loving, present in silicate phases)
Atmophile (volatile gases of the atmosphere)
solution: Goldschmidt's classes: lithophile (Si, Al, K), siderophile (Fe, Ni, Au), chalcophile (Cu, Pb, Zn, S) and atmophile (N, noble gases). Chalcophiles concentrate in sulfide phases.
